clue.text: Bounced off after being fired

parts.note: describes what a bullet or shell does when it glances off a surface once it has left the gun

explanation.surface: A projectile skims off a wall after the shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet that glances off a hard surface and flies on at an angle is said to have done this.

clue.text: Stagger to the dance

explanation.surface: Someone lurches unsteadily towards the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger is to totter or sway, and a lively Scottish country dance has the same name.

clue.text: Bells to the artist are a fanciful conception

parts.note: a chime is a set of tuned bells
RA stands for Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Ringing bells strike a painter as a mere flight of imagination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' simply joins the pieces: CHIME placed beside RA.
explanation.definitionFit: In everyday use the word means an illusion or wild fancy, from the fire-breathing monster of Greek myth.

clue.text: Mad young M.D., cruel and churlish

indicators.note: something mad is wild and disordered, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order

parts.note: MD, Doctor of Medicine, taken as its two letters

explanation.surface: A crazed junior doctor is unkind and rude to patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' looks like part of the description of the doctor, but it tells you to rearrange YOUNG, MD and CRUEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A churlish, bad-tempered old grump is exactly the type described by this adjective.

clue.text: Authorizes me to go up to wartime captives without hesitation

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the word me is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as the word itself

indicators.note: in its old sense of outside, so the captives stand around the hesitation

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: An official permits the writer to visit prisoners of war straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without hesitation' reads as 'immediately', but 'without' means outside: POWS wraps ER, after EM from 'me to go up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean giving someone the official right or power to act.

clue.text: Draw out Samuel's mentor about it

parts.note: in the Bible the boy Samuel was brought up in the temple by the priest Eli
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone coaxes the story of the prophet's teacher out of a witness.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw out a response or information from someone is to evoke or extract it.

clue.text: Element found in Santa Cruz in California

indicators.note: says the answer is found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A mineral is discovered in a Californian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'Cruz in California'.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallic chemical element, symbol Zn, used for galvanising iron.

clue.text: I caught an antelope in the country

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A hunter boasts of bagging a buck out in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nordic island nation in the North Atlantic, capital Reykjavik.

clue.text: Auditors granting a loan to Antony

definitions.text: Auditors granting a loan to Antony

parts.words: Auditors granting a loan to Antony
parts.note: recalls the funeral speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar where Mark Antony asks his hearers to lend him their ears

explanation.surface: Accountants advance money to a man called Antony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' suggests accountants, but it means listeners; 'granting a loan' is lending their ears, as Antony begs in 'Friends, Romans, ...'.
explanation.definitionFit: Antony addresses his fellow Romans, his compatriots, as he asks them to lend him their ears.

clue.text: Like the inscription for which I charge Pip perhaps

indicators.note: signals that the following words might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A stonemason prices up the lettering on Pip's memorial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the letters of I CHARGE PIP.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to inscriptions carved on stone or coins.

clue.text: Tie, say, for a lover

indicators.note: asks for the word heard when bow is spoken

parts.note: a bow is a knot tied in ribbon or a bow tie

explanation.surface: A man wears a bow tie for his sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend or admirer.

clue.text: Perhaps I err with one costume which is showily attractive

indicators.note: suggests the letters could appear in a different order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An actor admits his outfit may be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' tells you to rearrange I ERR, I (for 'one') and COSTUME; 'which is' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flashy and tawdry, attractive on the surface but without real value.

clue.text: People with high-class following find it in a restaurant

indicators.note: the high-class letter comes after the people

parts.note: men are people
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Posh diners discover something in an eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: U as 'upper-class' comes from a 1950s British usage contrasting U and non-U speech.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of dishes on offer is what a diner looks at in an eating house.

clue.text: Innocent to torment small fry ?

parts.note: white suggests purity and innocence
to bait is to tease or torment

explanation.surface: Picking on the blameless little ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small fry' usually means unimportant people; here it means tiny fish, the young herring and sprats that are fried whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny young fish eaten whole are literally young fry of small size.

clue.text: He keeps an eye on runners who dodge their duty

definitions.text: He keeps an eye on runners who dodge their duty

parts.words: He keeps an eye on runners who dodge their duty
parts.note: the runners are smugglers who land goods to dodge customs duty, watched by a shore patrol officer

explanation.surface: A supervisor monitors athletes who skip work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are smugglers (rum-runners), not athletes, and 'duty' is customs duty, not an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shore patrol officer watched the shoreline to catch smugglers landing goods without paying customs.

clue.text: William's hot-house?

parts.note: plays on King William III, William of Orange, as if a glasshouse were named after him

explanation.surface: A man named William owns a heated greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: William of Orange, the Dutch prince who became William III of England, suggests a building for his namesake fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass building for growing citrus trees through the winter is a classic country-house feature.

clue.text: Belladonna is .so poisonous

explanation.surface: A plant is declared toxic.
explanation.walkthrough: Belladonna's common name is 'deadly nightshade', so the plant is described by this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna's common name is deadly nightshade, and the word plainly means lethal or highly toxic.

clue.text: Speak, for a change, about art shares

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the word art
the letters of speak are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An investor talks about his holdings in art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shares' looks like a noun (stocks), but it is the verb; 'for a change' turns SPEAK into PAKES, and 'about' puts it around ART.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake of something is to take a share in it along with others.

clue.text: Such service for the navy

parts.note: refers to the nickname given to Britain's Royal Navy as the oldest of the armed forces

explanation.surface: A kind of duty performed at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Navy, as the oldest of Britain's armed services, is called the Senior Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Senior Service is the traditional British nickname for the Royal Navy, older than the army or air force.

clue.text: Disgusting outcry>' about an honour awarded

indicators.note: the outcry is placed around the honour

parts.note: noise is clamour or an outcry
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: There is a revolting public protest over someone being given an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awarded' completes the surface and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something offensive or foul-smelling is repellent, nasty to the senses.

clue.text: Deportment which transports one

explanation.surface: Good bearing is what carries a person along.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage is the way one holds oneself, and also a horse-drawn vehicle or railway coach that conveys people.

clue.text: A writer's attribute

parts.note: a scribe is a writer or copyist

explanation.surface: A characteristic belonging to a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attribute' looks like a noun but is the verb, to credit something to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit a work or quality to someone is to assign it to them.

clue.text: Dirty little devil on the river

parts.note: an imp is a small demon or mischievous child
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A grubby urchin plays by the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, a frequent crossword river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclean or contaminated is not pure.

clue.text: Diver displays culpability about damaged mole

indicators.note: the culpability is placed around the other letters

parts.note: guilt is blameworthiness

indicators.note: the word mole is broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer shows remorse over a hurt animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' turns MOLE into LEMO, and 'about' puts GUILT around it. 'Diver' is a diving seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the auk family that dives deep for fish from cliff colonies.

clue.text: Socrates owed this bird to Aesculapius

definitions.text: Socrates owed this bird to Aesculapius

parts.words: Socrates owed this bird to Aesculapius
parts.note: recalls the philosopher's last words in Plato's Phaedo, asking that a sacrifice owed to the god of healing be paid

explanation.surface: A philosopher's debt of poultry to a god.
explanation.walkthrough: Socrates' last words, as Plato tells them, were 'Crito, we owe a cock to Asclepius; pay it.'
explanation.definitionFit: The male domestic fowl was the sacrifice Socrates asked to be offered to the healing god.

clue.text: Steer to enter a street

indicators.note: the word to goes into the street abbreviation

explanation.surface: Guide the vehicle into a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb, but it is a young bullock; stot is a northern and Scottish word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: A stot is a dialect word for a young castrated bullock, the animal also called a steer.

clue.text: Small matter for a Bedlamite

parts.note: a Tom o' Bedlam was a madman from the Bethlehem asylum in London

explanation.surface: A trifling concern for a lunatic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedlam was London's Bethlehem Hospital for the insane; its discharged inmates who begged were called Tom o' Bedlam.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest unit of a chemical element is a tiny particle of matter.

clue.text: Bird has a drink at the plant

parts.note: the cuckoo is a bird
a pint is a drink of beer

explanation.surface: A bird stops for a beer at the pub's garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lords-and-ladies, the wild arum, is a woodland plant also known by this name.

clue.text: Worms surely unsuitable for such a regimen?

definitions.text: Worms surely unsuitable for such a regimen?

parts.words: Worms surely unsuitable for such a regimen?
parts.note: Worms is the German city where Luther was tried in 1521 by an imperial assembly of the same name as an eating plan

explanation.surface: Eating worms hardly suits a weight-loss plan.
explanation.walkthrough: The Diet of Worms was the imperial assembly at the German city of Worms that condemned Luther; read with lower-case 'worms', it sounds like a nasty eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a regimen of eating, and also a formal assembly like the one held at Worms.

clue.text: Ten priests though tortured remain constant

indicators.note: the letters of the words are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Martyred clergy keep the faith under torture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tortured' tells you to rearrange TEN PRIESTS; 'though' and 'remain' complete the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone steadfast who keeps going without wavering is unrelenting.
